description: The plot illustrates how ACC (in percent) varies with the co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME), shown as separate lines. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and is displayed on a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\); four discrete x-positions are plotted, ranging from a leftmost single-digit co-occurrence value to a rightmost value in the several-thousand range. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from 60 to the mid-80s, with labeled ticks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 64 at the leftmost point to about 71 at the rightmost point (intermediate points near ~66.5 and ~69). FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 65.2 to about 73.1 (with intermediate values around ~68.9 and ~71.5). IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 67.5 to about 75.2 (intermediate values around ~71.8 and ~74.3). MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, moving upward from about 70.6 to about 80.1 (intermediate values around ~75.6 and ~78.3). MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon-like markers, increasing from about 69.6 to about 77.7 (intermediate values around ~73.7 and ~76.9). ROME is a green solid line with square markers, rising from about 74.2 to about 84.6 (intermediate values around ~79.5 and ~82.2).
